# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

First iteration off the seed (LEDGER/JOURNAL empty). All 21 failing tasks "produced an output
file but values did not match" — no environment fault (val 0.580 has real capability signal).
Diagnosed all 21 trajectories with 3 parallel read-only subagents (batches of 7). Findings
converged on two clean, prompt-fixable clusters plus a hard logic cluster.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Type contract (both directions) | 50630, 57232 (num/date where TEXT expected) + 56427, 51958, 55931 (text where NUMBER/DATE expected) | Agent picks wrong python type; scorer compares value AND type → right value, wrong type = 0. Scorer feedback literally states the two rules. | KNOWLEDGE / OUTPUT-CONTRACT | Explicit dual type-contract rule at point of use + verify-step type check |
| 2 | Live formula not recalc-verified | 53367 (ArrayFormula), 47741 (TEXTJOIN/_xlfn), 56637 (formula→"" blanks), 59743, 56996 (RANDBETWEEN, unwinnable) | Agent writes live formula, "verifies" by printing formula TEXT; some funcs don't recalc headlessly → blank/stale; volatile inputs unmatchable. | KNOWLEDGE + BEHAVIORAL(verify) | Additive knowledge on recalc + verify-step recalc check |
| 3 | Fabricated / unstated criterion | 11842 (÷2 invented), 5192 (invented char-strip), helps 39046/51359 | Agent invents a normalization the instruction never states. | KNOWLEDGE | Anti-fabrication rule + reproduce-the-example check |
| — | Genuinely hard/ambiguous logic or reference quirks | 3911, 5192, 30709, 325-44, 450-9, 57090, 59259 | Under-specified rule / Excel locale-DATEVALUE quirk / greedy-allocation ambiguity | CAPABILITY-GAP | SKIPPED — not prose-fixable without hardcoding the answer |

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Tighten output contract (dual, at point of use) | task_template.md ("Match the expected TYPE") | States the scorer's own two rules: TEXT answer → keep string, don't parse; NUMBER/DATE answer → real int/float/datetime, not text form; when unsure copy the column's existing/example type. General across all cell types. | Yes — clarifies a contract passing tasks already satisfy; datetime-passers 110-2/41297 keep dates, text-passers keep text |
| 1 | Structural checklist (precondition to finish) | task_template.md (verify step 3b) | Verify step must reject a str-where-number (or number-where-text) mismatch and rewrite — turns the type contract into an unavoidable pre-finish gate. | Yes — passing tasks already produce correct types, check is a no-op for them |
| 2 | Add missing knowledge (grounded in grader) | task_template.md (new "Formulas are graded by RECALCULATED value" block) | Explains headless-LibreOffice recalc; plain cell formulas OK (keep them); «redacted» don't recalc → write literal; ""→blank lowers coverage. | Yes — the 4 passing formula tasks use plain IF/INDEX/SUMIFS/WORKDAY/CF-rule, none in the "won't recalc" list; explicitly told to KEEP plain formulas so literalization pressure is reduced, protecting per-copy-tracking answers |
| 2 | Structural checklist | task_template.md (verify step 3c) | For a formula answer, recompute the result in python and confirm recalc value (not the text) and that it isn't blank. | Yes — no-op for passing tasks whose formulas already recalc correctly |
| 3 | Add missing rule + example-reproduction check | prompt.md (new bullet) + task_template.md (verify step 3d) | Apply only stated operations; don't invent ÷/strip/reformat; when a worked example exists, pick the interpretation that reproduces it exactly. | Yes — passing tasks don't over-transform; rule fires only when agent would invent an unstated step |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change → the trace it targets)
- 50630/57232: scorer feedback "where a str is expected, KEEP the original text — do not parse or convert" → new TEXT-contract bullet + verify 3b would have kept the split substring / looked-up code as str instead of datetime/float. Value already correct; only type was wrong.
- 56427/51958/55931: scorer feedback "where a number or date is expected, write the real typed value rather than its text form" → new NUMBER/DATE bullet + verify 3b would have written int/float/datetime instead of str '1.3'/'09/08/21'/'#N/A'. Encodes the scorer's own rule (verified against scorer output, not just old prompt).
- 53367: agent wrote openpyxl ArrayFormula and verified only the formula text; new recalc block lists ArrayFormula as non-recalculating → compute literal boolean instead; verify 3c would have caught it. 55667's plain SUMPRODUCT cell-formula (passing) is NOT ArrayFormula and NOT listed → unaffected.
- 47741: TEXTJOIN/_xlfn live formula; recalc block names TEXTJOIN → write literal short-date string matching the worked-example format.
- 56637: formula returned "" for out-of-range rows (coverage 91/146); "" -> blank note + verify would flag underfilled coverage.
- 56996: RANDBETWEEN source is unwinnable — recalc block names it so the agent recognizes and reports rather than burning turns (documented as unwinnable).
- 11842/5192: agent invented "half-day → ÷2" and a char-strip heuristic; anti-fabrication bullet + verify 3d (reproduce the worked example exactly) push it to the interpretation matching the example.

## Blast-radius summary (which class, named passing tasks)
- All edits are BOUNDED/ADDITIVE — clarifications of the value+type output contract and additive knowledge, applying only under conditions present in the failing cases.
- Formula edit checked against every passing formula task: CF_11072 (conditional-formatting rule, governed separately), 55060 (=IF), 55667 (=INDEX/SUMPRODUCT), 58109 (=SUMIFS/WORKDAY) — none use «redacted», and plain formulas are explicitly told to stay. No forced literalization of per-copy-tracking formulas.
- Type edit checked against datetime-passers 110-2, 41297 (dates stay dates) and text-producing passers (str stays str). No global decision/permission rule touched.

## Process & features used
- Subagents: 3 parallel general-purpose read-only subagents, one per 7-task batch, to diagnose all 21 failing trajectories concurrently; synthesized their reports into the 3 clusters. Edits applied serially by me (surgical, non-conflicting — no worktrees needed).
- Prior iterations: none (first off seed). Cross-checked auto-memory: honored "no blanket strip" (type rule is provenance/semantic, not stripping), "don't ban formulas / keep formula guidance verbatim" (plain formulas kept; only non-recalculating funcs redirected), "recalc via LibreOffice exotic-func exception" (basis for Edit 2).

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The dual type-contract wording mirrors the SCORER's own feedback strings — do not soften to a single direction.
- The explicit "plain formulas are fine, keep them" clause — removing it risks over-literalizing 55060/55667/58109 (their correct answer is a live per-copy formula).

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- Hard logic/criterion gaps and reference quirks: 3911 (ambiguous greedy allocation, failed the PREVIEW copy), 30709 (Excel locale DATEVALUE quirk baked into GT), 325-44 / 450-9 (exact expansion/label-sequence semantics), 57090 (dedup counting rule), 59259 (2/3 near-miss, one-variant edge). Prose can't fix these without hardcoding the gold answer → overfitting. The Edit-3 anti-fabrication + example-reproduction check gives partial coverage (11842, 5192, 39046, 51359) without hardcoding.
